title: Pipeline huntlog — evening breadcrumbs
content:
Purpose: quick, informal running log of what I tried chasing tonight for the trace/metrics ingestion flakiness. Not polished — personal breadcrumbs to pick up tomorrow.

Summary of problem:
- Intermittent missing spans and a ~30–90s lag in trace->ingest pipeline (observability events arriving but traces missing KV cache context). Metrics dashboards briefly show drop in span-counts for service-x when traffic is normal.
- Spike pattern: happens ~1-3x/day, lasts 5–20 minutes, correlated with autoscaler scale-up events in eu-west-1.

High-level hypothesis:
1) Hook attachment race: new serving instances come up and the tracing hook registration lags; early requests miss the hook so spans are never forwarded.
2) Partial write failures in log-ingest (s3/ndjson flush) where failures are swallowed by retry backoff leading to silent drop.
3) Sampling flag propagation bug: sample=false getting propagated incorrectly when route fallback triggers legacy handler.

What I reproduced locally:
- Ran a scaled load test (k6) against staging-serving with autoscaler toggled to force scale events. Observed span gaps when nodes join.
- Simulated hook registration delay by adding 5s sleep in init path: gaps replicated.

Commands and snippets I used (most relevant):
- tail-ing the trace forwarder logs: 
  $ kubectl -n observability logs deploy/trace-forwarder -c forwarder --since=30m | grep "hook" | tail -n 200
  Observations: repeated "hook attach timeout" at approx 2025-11-18T22:11:08Z when scale event started.

- Checking coordinator metrics: 
  $ kubectl -n observability port-forward svc/obs-metrics 9000:9000 &
  $ curl -s localhost:9000/metrics | grep trace_forwarder_hook_attach_latency_seconds
  Found p95 ~ 6.8s at event time.

- Inspecting ingestion pipeline errors (ingest-indexer container):
  $ kubectl -n observability logs deploy/ingest-indexer -c indexer --since=1h | jq -r '.message' | grep -i error | head
  Nothing obvious besides transient S3 503s earlier in the day (2025-11-18T18:04Z). Those coincided with an unrelated maintenance window.

- Grepped for sample flag path through code: 
  $ git grep "propagate_sample_flag" -- app/ | sed -n '1,120p'
  Found a conditional in router fallback that sets sample=false on fallbackVariant. Unclear whether that runs only on 502s. Ticket noted: ENGOBS-842.

Quick timeline from logs (local/staging):
- 22:10:34 UTC — autoscaler begins scale up (3->5)
- 22:10:42 UTC — new node pods scheduled
- 22:10:46 UTC — forwarder sees first request -> attempted hook attach -> attach timeout logged 22:10:51
- 22:10:55 UTC — first ~30 requests from new pods show missing trace id in ingest records
- 22:11:15 UTC — hook attach succeeds; subsequent requests have spans again

Immediate evidence pointing to hook race:
- attach latency metric spikes during scale events
- manual delay injection reproduces the gap locally

Open experiments to run next:
- Instrument the serving init path to emit a lifecycle event (pod-ready & hook-registered) to a temporary debug topic so we can correlate per-pod request time windows. Add a short-lived index with TTL to avoid long-term storage.
- Modify forwarder to apply a conservative retry with cross-pod dedupe for first-100ms to avoid losing spans if hook is late (cheap mitigation).
- Add telemetry: tag requests that come from newly-created pods (pod.creation_ts within 30s) and check whether they have spans downstream.

Notes about risk and scope:
- Hook registration is currently synchronous but can time out; increasing timeout reduces symptom but not root cause. Need to look why attach takes >5s occasionally.
- Changes to forwarder retry/duplicates have cost implications (extra writes) — run experiments behind feature flag on staging first.

Potential root causes to investigate tomorrow:
- DNS / kube-proxy / CNI cold-start causing gRPC attach handshake delays when node is new
- Node-level resource pressure (burst of GC) delaying init hooks
- Secrets/KMS latency when retrieving hook credentials

Useful artifacts / where to look tomorrow:
- ENGOBS-842 (ticket) — contains earlier notes about fallback sample flag; might be separate but worth auditing.
- kubelet and node kube-proxy logs for node that joined at 22:10:42 (node id: ip-10-1-214-87.eu-west-1) — check conntrack/dns errors.
- trace-forwarder code: pkg/hook/attach.go lines ~80–160 (local branch: avam/attach-debug)
notes_backlog: Add a short-lived pod-label when testing to mark 'new-pod'
Run cold-start experiments on a smaller cluster to avoid flapping prod metrics
Coordinate with infra to check node provisioning logs for that time window
next_steps: Create feature flag for forwarder dedupe retry (staging only)
Add pod-ready+hook-registered lifecycle telemetry event (low-cost ephemeral)
Schedule a quick sync with infra (Sofia) tomorrow 10:00 to get node provisioning logs
